Canonical conversion selection retains literal text and native Visio diagram defaults when the semantic Reader routes are also registered. The same private selection rule is used by the front door and Workflows. Shared bounded-output markers remain identifiable through conversion exception chains.

Conversion sidecars are privately staged until report acceptance. Final-output failures retain completed source diagnostics through one internal shared helper; cancellation remains cancellation. Adapter plumbing uses InternalsVisibleTo rather than new public members.
The diagnostic catalog contract test checks the real legacy chart-projected entry mapping to ChartFlattened. It no longer assumes that the new catalog spelling was itself a legacy producer code.

The existing OfficeChartSeries model becomes root OfficeIMO.OfficeSeries, adding numeric typed-selector factories. OfficeChartKind merges into the M1 OfficeChartType enum. Native chart writers and all in-repo type consumers use that single enum/model; typed and nameof-based AddChart overloads reuse the existing shared native chart data pipeline. Core builds on all three macOS targets with zero warnings; six typed native chart artifact cases and 166 shared chart regression cases pass on each modern framework.
OfficeCalloutKind (Info, Success, Warning, Danger) preserves the removed Word fluent callout capability through typed theme intent.

extraChanges.subject: Extensible shared table options
extraChanges.note: OfficeTableOptions supports format-specific options through inheritance; ExcelTableOptions retains nested projection and native table presentation settings.

The generated public-surface candidate list is applied. Undocumented native/parser plumbing is internal; documented options, results, interfaces and model data remain public. The seven Tier1 packages ship compiler-generated nullable PublicAPI baselines and pass API/XML analysis on the declared host targets.

OfficeTableOptions absorbs the Markdown projection controls. Declared-row projection applies selection before bounds and supports generic/read-only dictionaries through the existing dictionary adapter. Projection snapshots copy formatter dictionaries so native table overrides do not mutate reusable options. Empty dictionary-interface sequences are rejected without exposing dictionary metadata as columns. Display headers remain independent of unique source member names.

Visibility analysis retains public value-type contracts, exposed model constructors and immutable With copies. The generated candidate list no longer proposes hiding OfficeLength unit conversions or OfficeTheme model construction; private native constructors remain private. This changes the candidate analysis, not the M1 public API.

Visibility analysis distinguishes immutable model construction from attachment plumbing: an undocumented constructor requiring a format document remains a candidate. Explicit construction examples still retain their constructors. The generated Word image constructor candidates are reviewed against the canonical AddImage entry points; foundation model construction stays public.

extraChanges.change: Visibility analysis follows cross-format C# and PowerShell examples, Markdown syntax nodes, exceptions, attributes, virtual contracts and concrete subclasses of exposed abstract models.
extraChanges.reason: Documentation and public model closure determine candidates. Concrete field/drawing/syntax nodes remain usable when returned through an abstract base; caller catch/attribute/override contracts are not private implementation plumbing.

extraChanges.change: 43 undocumented static helper types are internal after generated candidate review.
extraChanges.reason: These types implement rendering, parsing, package metadata or serialization behind the documented object model. Public models, syntax nodes, exceptions, attributes and virtual contracts remain visible.

extraChanges.change: Implementation access to internal helpers uses explicit friend assemblies.
extraChanges.reason: Callers were identified from actual C# identifier syntax in existing projects. Public third-party plug-in contracts remain public and receive no friend access.

extraChanges.change: Public API declarations and nullable annotations are enforced against shipped compiler baselines.
extraChanges.reason: The private Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers build asset rejects unrecorded additions and removals without adding a runtime dependency. Existing framework-specific APIs retain separate shipped baselines where needed; target declarations and restore locks are unchanged.

extraChanges.change: Generated diagnostic constants explicitly enable nullable annotations.
extraChanges.reason: Generated sources need their own nullable context so diagnostic string constants match the non-null public contract. The catalog values are unchanged.

extraChanges.change: The baseline bootstrap reads both compiler SARIF message representations.
extraChanges.reason: The compiler default SARIF uses string messages; SARIF 2.1 uses message.text. Both feed the same RS0016-only baseline generator without changing source or suppressing diagnostics.

extraChanges.change: Maintained Windows and non-Windows package locks include the public API analyzer.
extraChanges.reason: Refreshes the existing release restore graphs for the private build dependency, preserving their runtime identifiers, framework sets and platform-selection mechanism.

extraChanges.change: DBF-to-XLSX route entry point uses CreateWriter(...).WriteTable(name, reader).
extraChanges.reason: The retired static ExcelDocument.WriteDataReader entry point no longer exists. Catalog projections retain the same route and fidelity.

extraChanges.change: Image execution and persistence move from fluent bases into internal shared operations. Format, FileConflictPolicy and FailOnLoss are image options; eight shared renderer codes join the M1 diagnostic catalog. Conversion evidence preserves severity, loss, location and source format independently.
extraChanges.reason: The Tier 1 public image builders can be removed without duplicating execution code or removing the shared bases still used by Tier 2 packages.

extraChanges.change: The DOCX image routes identify OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf as their owning package, matching the moved Word page renderer. Compatibility artifacts and README projections are regenerated from the catalog.
extraChanges.reason: Mechanical consumer closure and shared-owner preservation for the approved API change.

extraChanges.new: Current source conversion, typed geometry and diagnostic APIs
extraChanges.reason: The native conversion corpus uses the canonical font-family-substitution diagnostic constant.

extraChanges.change: Close full-solution consumers of the unified API
extraChanges.reason: The shared managed-font fixture requires the internal text-element enumerator in OfficeIMO.Tool.Tests; an explicit test friend keeps that plumbing internal.

extraChanges.change: Describe PDF image conversion through the public byte and report contract
extraChanges.reason: The capability source catalog uses PdfDocument.ExportImages with PdfImageExportOptions and OfficeConversionReport. All five PDF image routes describe IReadOnlyList<byte[]>; detailed per-page results remain internal host plumbing. Generated compatibility and website route projections follow this catalog.

extraChanges.change: Write canonical chart identifiers for Column/Bar convenience aliases in HTML and Reader JSON.
extraChanges.reason: The broader net8 PowerPoint HTML suite reproduced Enum.ToString selecting Column instead of ColumnClustered. One internal shared-source formatter now gives ColumnClustered/BarClustered consistently to PowerPoint HTML, Excel HTML and PowerPoint Reader payloads, including per-series kinds. Existing positioned HTML and rich Reader artifact tests cover the observable identifiers. No public helper or external dependency is added.
extraChanges.note: The shared-source package guardrail includes the internal chart-name formatter in its approved infrastructure list.

extraChanges.change: Limit the ToHashSet compatibility extension to netstandard2.0
extraChanges.reason: The .NET Framework 4.7.2 BCL already provides ToHashSet. Compiling the full net472 Workflows graph exposed ambiguous comparer overloads when the fallback was also visible. Other older-framework fallbacks remain available.

extraChanges.change: Retain normalized RGB literals in the canonical OfficeColor value type.
extraChanges.reason: The single public color contract preserves existing normalized PDF authoring precision without changing byte channel units, role resolution or hexadecimal/CSS byte projections. Exact byte fractions keep byte equality and hash values; other precise literals retain exact RGB channels in unmanaged value storage.
extraChanges.note: Core and Drawing.Tests are qualified on net8.0/net10.0, with netstandard2.0 and net472 compilation. The PDF public color migration remains separate.
extraChanges.notes: Normalized RGB literals retain exact finite channels in unmanaged value storage. Byte getters and hexadecimal/CSS formatting remain byte projections. Exact byte fractions retain existing equality and hash values; precise colors remain distinct cache keys. Alpha stays a byte. No new runtime dependency or framework change.

extraChanges.new: Concrete source-document ToImage / SaveAsImage / SaveAsImages with format options; existing internal image operations
extraChanges.reason: Remove the fluent image surface while retaining format renderers, Core execution/persistence, streaming, deadlines, limits and diagnostic evidence.
extraChanges.qualification: Static preparation only. Parent applies and qualifies every maintained target; no build or test was run.

extraChanges.change: Map positional records through the shared automatic row plan
extraChanges.reason: Automatic reader, async, parallel and CSV projections bind an unambiguous public constructor after the existing property and alias resolution. Constructor values use the same conversions, culture, formats and redaction policy; mutable models retain the parameterless path. Explicit assignment maps keep their existing construction contract. Constructor metadata is preserved for trimming and NativeAOT. Getter-only constructor properties and record-struct primary constructors participate in the same plan; explicit public parameterless construction and plain mutable structs retain their paths. Missing mandatory constructor columns reject a constructor-bound value model instead of bypassing its validation through implicit default construction.
Add methods expose the created object. A repeated type-library identity returns its existing reference without changing native project bytes, name, path or edit state.

extraChanges.change: Align chart type/data/options order across Word, Excel and PowerPoint
extraChanges.reason: OfficeChartOptions owns the shared title and physical dimensions. Format options retain Word rounded corners, Excel one-based row/column anchors and PowerPoint position/accessibility. Typed and nameof projections accept options without duplicating data projection or chart rendering. Format defaults and editable native series are preserved.

extraChanges.old: ObjectFlattener ExpandRows raw collection cells; explicit projection columns bypassing common Order
extraChanges.new: Shared lazy per-element formatting/null policy and common ordering of selected explicit columns
extraChanges.reason: Typed tables in Excel, PowerPoint and PDF apply each formatter once to its actual cell value and respect common table ordering.
extraChanges.note: Expanded elements use the shared formatting/null policy once per cell. Explicit column ordering retains its selection whitelist even when filters select no columns. PDF native projection regressions and Word creation/spacing regressions pass on net10.0; full framework/AOT gates remain separate.

extraChanges.old: OfficeTheme chart/table tokens and five hand-authored built-in theme definitions
extraChanges.new: OfficeTheme text styles, paragraph spacing, rules, surfaces, page/footer settings and extended chart/table tokens; generated built-ins from Build/Visual/themes.json
extraChanges.reason: Creation options and native table/layout defaults share the full immutable visual identity instead of format-local constants.
extraChanges.note: Keep existing seven-component construction and normalized color semantics. Generated nullable source and all four shipped baselines build cleanly. Word native theme/table and PDF projection suites pass on net10.0; remaining format, AOT and framework gates are separate.

extraChanges.old: OfficeChartSnapshot constructors and WithSize(double widthPoints, double heightPoints), WidthPoints and HeightPoints
extraChanges.new: OfficeChartSnapshot constructors and WithSize(OfficeLength width, OfficeLength height), Width and Height
extraChanges.reason: Shared chart snapshots are caller-visible geometry and use the same physical length contract as native authoring. Rendering converts to points at the drawing boundary.
extraChanges.note: All explicit snapshot constructors and resize consumers use typed lengths; positive-size validation and immutable chart metadata remain. Exact EMUs survive construction and resize.

extraChanges.old: Shared series and point outline/stroke widths, OfficeDiagramSnapshot WidthPoints/HeightPoints, redundant binary-compatible CreateBubble overload. Original OfficeChartStyle and OfficeChartPointStyle binary-signature constructor wrappers.
extraChanges.new: OfficeLength physical outline/stroke widths; diagram Width/Height use lengths. CreateBubble has one canonical factory with optional outline visibility.
extraChanges.reason: Shared native chart/diagram geometry uses physical lengths; drawing-coordinate font descriptors preserve unquantized local units required by DPI-scaled and nested mathematical layout.
extraChanges.note: OfficeFontInfo.Size and its numeric constructor/WithSize remain contextual drawing units. Runtime math contracts disproved the earlier physical-size classification; no drawing-unit-to-EMU quantization or duplicate descriptor is introduced. Remove the obsolete binary-compatible bubble factory and original point-style constructor and reflection pin; retain existing default/explicit-outline behavior assertions. MarkerSize is undergoing a separate source-unit review. The two OfficeChartStyle compiled-signature wrappers and their reflection-only constructor-count fact are removed; canonical creation contracts and behavior tests remain.

extraChanges.new: OfficeFontInfo.Size remains double in drawing coordinate units
extraChanges.reason: DPI-scaled em sizes and nested math fractions are contextual local geometry, like OfficeDrawing paths and coordinates. Public physical document font APIs remain OfficeLength.

extraChanges.old: Numeric imported point/series outline metadata converted without checking the physical representation.
extraChanges.new: HTML and ODF readers reject nonfinite, out-of-bounds or zero-after-quantization outline widths through their existing omission/unprojected-appearance paths.
extraChanges.reason: Untrusted chart metadata must not throw during physical length conversion or prevent native chart enumeration.

extraChanges.old: OfficeSeries.MarkerSize nullable integer points and markerSize constructor parameter.
extraChanges.new: OfficeLength? marker diameter retained through shared snapshots, rendering and native adapters.
extraChanges.reason: Shared chart markers follow the physical length contract without rounding fractional points before native serialization.
extraChanges.note: Core retains positive sizes without a native upper cap, null and exact EMUs through copies. Native writers preserve their existing format minimum/72-point maximum and round whole points away from zero. Contextual drawing font sizes stay numeric; no earlier font proposal or compatibility wrapper is restored.

extraChanges.old: OfficePageSize(double widthInches, double heightInches), WidthInches/HeightInches and unit-specific conversion factories/helpers.
extraChanges.new: OfficePageSize(OfficeLength width, OfficeLength height), typed Width/Height; read units through OfficeLength.
extraChanges.reason: A physical page size carries explicit units consistently with document and image export geometry.
extraChanges.note: Remove FromMillimeters and ToPointWidth/ToPointHeight convenience helpers; consumers construct Millimeters/Inches lengths and read Width.ToPoints or Height.ToPoints. Portrait/landscape use typed lengths. Raster DPI/scale stay numeric with existing ceiling/minimum-pixel behavior. Preserve native artifact assertions, relative geometry and contextual font sizes; no aliases or golden changes.

extraChanges.reason: Absolute authoring stroke width is a physical length; null retains numeric WidthFontFraction. Drawing Scale stays unquantized numerical render state.
extraChanges.note: Existing absolute double.Epsilon/double.MaxValue theory moved to relative WidthFontFraction with original rows and bounded-paint/body/field assertions; expected immutable declaration is fraction plus null Width. Tiny absolute dotted fixture becomes one EMU. Absolute finite 0/-1 guards retained; impossible nonfinite absolute branch retired, all relative invalid-value checks retained. Numeric drawing coordinates, relative ratios, resource pixel counts and measured concealment thresholds remain unchanged.

extraChanges.reason: Absolute authored leader font size is physical; null retains FontSizeFactor. Resolved drawing font sizes, Scale/Tint override state and OfficeFontInfo remain numerical.
extraChanges.note: Keep absolute 15/20/30-point expectations as exact typed lengths and all fitting/body/field/ODF assertions. Keep physical finite 0/-1 and all relative invalid-value guards; retire only impossible absolute NaN/Infinity assignments. Numeric drawing coordinates, relative ratios, resource pixel counts and measured concealment thresholds remain unchanged.

extraChanges.new: Keep native declarations unchanged and project positive sub-EMU sizes as one EMU, reporting the shared rendering approximation.

extraChanges.note: Saved ODG line/text controls fail before the fix. Preserve source XML, body text and tab positions; finite zero/negative and nonfinite validation is unchanged. Native values outside OfficeLength range retain the existing explicit unsupported path.

extraChanges.old: PDF image capability entries describe byte-array page results.
extraChanges.new: Both PDF image entries describe IReadOnlyList<OfficeImageExportResult>.
extraChanges.reason: The executable capability contract must match the canonical PDF export facade.

The content-safety classifier threshold is a physical font size. Preserve the inclusive zero-to-72-point option range and existing per-format native comparisons through ToPoints at their numeric boundary.
extraChanges.note: All native classifier scaling, risk ordering, evidence and exact defaults remain. Nonfinite values are rejected by the shared length factory before option assignment; finite negative and above-range values remain rejected by option validation. No PDF user-space reinterpretation is made.

extraChanges.reason: Read the referenced DrawingML palette and Latin heading/body fonts from DOCX/DOTX, XLSX/XLTX or PPTX/POTX without copying document content. PowerPoint uses its first declared slide master; composition sizes and spacing retain Modern defaults.
